item.title: Asia’s Problems Are Outgrowing Its Summits
item.description: If there was ever a time for Southeast Asian nations to display some unity, it’s now. Summit season has arrived, right in the middle of the latest polycrisis. The US-Iran conflict has exposed the weakness of the region’s energy security plans, while the fragile ceasefire between Thailand and Cambodia, Myanmar’s military regime, a vast network of scam centers, and China’s maritime dominance remain key stressors.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Pollard

item.title: Van Hollen Isn’t the Fresh Face Democrats Need
item.description: For the first time in three decades, the race for who will lead Senate Democrats will be contested. This is a good development, a sign of a healthy, big-tent party — not at war with itself but grappling with what it stands for and where it is headed. I argued in a previous column that Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, 75, should stand down no matter the outcome of this month’s elections. I now think, given the party’s massive victories and the alternative to Schumer, he should stay on for two more
item.dc:creator: Nia-Malika Henderson

item.title: McRib Lawsuit Against McDonald’s Puts Mystery Meat History in Perspective
item.description: It is with an almost religious devotion that many Americans greet the resurrection of the famed McRib. For decades, McDonald’s has intermittently revived this iconic sandwich for a limited time only, enabling the faithful a little taste of heaven: 500-plus calories’ worth of ground pork extruded into a loose facsimile of some ribs, topped with barbecue sauce, pickles, and onions.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Mihm

item.title: Druski’s Rise to Netflix and SNL Shows a New Path for Black Creators
item.description: At the beginning of his Saturday Night Live monologue, comedian Druski nodded to his roots as a digital creator, which made his hosting gig historic: “Apparently, people are saying I'm the first internet-content-creator-social-media-influencer-only-make-you-laugh-on-your-phone-TikTok-and-YouTube-and-Instagram star to host this show.”
item.dc:creator: Peter A. Berry

item.title: Senate Democrats, Please Show a Little Discipline
item.description: Fresh off their sweeping midterm victory, Democrats almost immediately got mired in an inconvenient Senate leadership fight. It’s part of a larger squabble over who got the greater mandate in the midterms — moderates or progressives. But voters don’t give a hoot about factions or infighting. They simply want to see their lives improve.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: White House Threats Against Congress Are Constitutionally Preposterous
item.description: A preview of the constitutional struggle that lies ahead arrived at the Capitol last week on White House letterhead. In a letter sent to Representative Robert Garcia, the California Democrat who will be chairing the House Oversight Committee next year, White House Counsel William Scharf warned that congressional oversight “may cross the line into blatant criminality.” Later, asked if the White House would comply with congressional subpoenas, he told Bloomberg News: “It depends,” adding that the
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: The Climate Change Fight: Why the World Needs to Rethink
item.description: This is the first of three editorials about why the fight against climate change is failing, and what to do about it.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: AI's Climate Change Will Destroy the Global Village to Save It
item.description: Not long ago, there was this idea that artificial intelligence could help the planet avoid the worst of global heating by using its superior brainpower to discover climate solutions humans couldn’t. Lately, though, it seems that if AI is still going to save the global village, it will first have to destroy it. With climate change.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: Questions Around Howard Lutnick and Nvidia Keep Growing
item.description: Donald Trump exited his first term as president believing that he had surrounded himself with advisers who were more loyal to the Constitution or their own agendas than to him. He was determined not to make that mistake again when he began his second White House tour. Enter Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: FAA Flight Disruptions Need More Than Money to Fix
item.description: If you listened to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy explain why flights were grounded for about four hours on Friday, you would come away thinking that a lack of funding from Congress was the culprit. That’s not the case.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Jensen Huang Returning to Nvidia Would Ruin a Very Good Thing
item.description: You could argue that Jensen Huang’s ousting from Nvidia Corp. couldn’t have come at a worse time for the artificial intelligence trade. Anthropic PBC is going public on Thursday and the scandal has knocked confidence in a market already stretched by hype and expectation. Yet history may look back on this moment as a healthy one, when the AI boom finally entered an era of accountability and companies started to grow up.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: Nike Should End Its Partnership With Kim Kardashian's Skims
item.description: It’s time for Nike Inc. to break up with Kim Kardashian.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: NEETs Crisis: Britain's 10-Year Plan Is Like an Old Soviet Joke
item.description: Stung by Kemi Badenoch’s taunt that his “10-Year Plan for Government” is so airy that it had to be shuffled off to Boston Consulting Group to be written, Prime Minister Andy Burnham will rush out his blueprint for Britain before Christmas.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: After the Huang Scandal, AIndicators Look Shakier
item.description: Can Anthropic’s IPO reverse AI’s poor current momentum?
item.dc:creator: John Authers and Richard Abbey

item.title: Investors: Europe Is Doing OK Despite What Social Media Says
item.description: Whenever good news arrives from Europe — yes, that Europe — it can feel like a glitch in the matrix. Last week’s upbeat growth figure for the British economy, driven by artificial intelligence and government spending, caused Deutsche Bank Head of Macro Research Jim Reid to flag that the “global view of the UK invariably seems much more bearish than the reality.”
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Corporate Reforms Need to Go Further to End the Korea Stock Discount
item.description: South Korea’s stock exchange operator unveiled an inaugural list earlier this month of more than 100 companies with persistently low valuations. It’s a welcome step to address the chronic underpricing of the nation’s stocks. But it won’t be enough.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.title: American Support for Taiwan Looks Alarmingly Fragile
item.description: Donald Trump has been humiliated in the midterms, but his ability to exploit American might to cause grief abroad is not much diminished. US policy toward Iran remains uncertain, probably even in the White House. The administration is persisting in its attempts to sell Ukraine to Russia. Trump’s threats against Cuba linger.
item.dc:creator: Max Hastings
